messages:
morgan: Heads-up: last 3 hours we've had ~240 alerts from 'kms-access-fail' rule. Most are coming from service-account key rotations after yesterday's RBAC change. Feels like noise — drowning out real auth anomalies.

devon: Ack. I pulled a sample — they're all 403s with message 'key rotation in progress'. CI job pinging KMS. Can you paste sample event IDs?

morgan: sample IDs: evt-5c1a, evt-5c1b, evt-5c2f. Here's one event snippet:
```
user: svc-ci-runner
action: kms.decrypt
status: 403
message: key rotation in progress
```
Also dashboard alert triggered at 20/min threshold.

casey: We should tune rule to exclude service-account namespace or add exception for 'key rotation in progress'. Suggest changing detection from count>20/min to count>20/min AND distinct_users>3. That filters CI churn.

devon: Yep. Also propose 10m suppression window per service-account and add a visual that shows top 10 subjects. I'll open PR to rule repo. Query for elastic:
```
status:403 AND message:"key rotation in progress"
| stats count() by user
| where count > 20
```

morgan: :thumbsup: If we change to distinct_users>3 we don't block a real brute force that targets many accounts.

tara: Quick ops note: update runbook to include 'check KMS rotation schedule' and add a link to infra change ticket INFRA-472. Also ping product infra team to add tag on rotation jobs so SIEM can ignore them.

security-bot: Alert suppression policy updated: temporary mute for 'kms-access-fail' triggered by tag=rotation for 1h (by devon).

casey: PR: https://git.internal/rules/342 — adds exception and dashboard widget. I'm going to roll to staging. Will monitor for 30m and report back.

morgan: Thanks. Can someone also add a note in the SIEM dashboard description explaining the exception? new hires keep getting confused.

devon: Added dashboard note and folder README. rolling to prod in 40m if staging looks good.

tara: Perfect. Action items: casey—merge + prod roll; devon—suppression window + dashboard note; morgan—notify product infra about tagging; tara—update runbook. I'll follow up in #incidents after prod.
